links.outcome: Physician-rated clinical substance of chatbot answers in Hebrew versus English, within the same physicians
links.effect: The substance-minus-empathy gap narrowed from 0.92 to 0.44 and from 1.09 to 0.52 in the two English–Hebrew physicians, driven by lower substance in Hebrew.
links.quote: Empathy, the one cue a patient can judge, carried no information about whether the advice was safe, and clinical substance fell in Hebrew within both physicians who rated it.

unlisted_practices: Score clinical content independently of empathy when evaluating patient-facing chatbots
Evaluate chatbot clinical quality separately in each deployment language
Anchor chatbot evaluation on high-risk scenarios rather than any single product

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of commercial consumer LLM chatbots answering simulated patient scenarios across six languages, evaluated by physicians for safety, accuracy, and empathy.
